articles.title: NFL legend John Madden’s unlikely, unfiltered brilliance: ‘Coach was indeed animated’
articles.summary: With the release of a new David O Russell biopic about the coach turned commentator turned gaming icon, those who knew him best remember his singular career Wearing his Oakland Raiders uniform and helmet, and gripping an orange traffic cone like a lance, Ted Hendricks rode into the training session on a roan horse and stopped at the 50-yard line. Some American football coaches might have reacted to the stunt with fury. But John Madden was unfazed. “We needed some relief from the intense grind,” recalls Hendricks, 79, who had borrowed the horse from a nearby stable. “It was a spur of the moment idea, but put a smile on everyone’s face. articles.title: Now get out of that! How can the new James Bond film get around 007’s death in No Time to Die?
articles.summary: Was it all a dream? Has Bond been in hiding? Or will Robert Pattinson simply report to HR on his first day? Russell T Davies, David Hare and more give their takes “James Bond will return,” says the closing title on No Time to Die, the most recent James Bond film and the final one to star Daniel Craig. It is just as well: Bond has to all appearances been vaporised by sea-launched missiles, having been infected by nanobots programmed to attack his nearest and dearest at the slightest touch. No one would believe that one of the world’s most successful film series would come to such an abrupt halt, but no doubt a little reassurance helped. Nevertheless, the first order of business for scriptwriter Steven Knight and director Denis Villeneuve will be dealing with it: how to revive and re-energise a character at the heart of the action. articles.title: The week’s best new tracks and the act you need to know: the rangy folk-prog songwriting of Threshold
articles.summary: Isaac Eiger’s solo venture leaves jangle pop behind for a wilder sound. Often it owes a debt to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days? From New York via Montana Recommended if you like Cameron Winter, Tobias Jesso Jr, Alex G Up next Supporting Caroline on tour in Canada and the US until 19 November Isaac Eiger is something of a scene legend in the world of American indie-rock. Raised in Bozeman, Montana, he was the founder and lead singer of the cult shoegaze-adjacent six-piece Strange Ranger, who left heartbroken a small, fervent fanbase when they announced their breakup in 2023. Taking a discernibly British approach to their sound, Strange Ranger traversed C86-y jangle-pop before landing on Madchester rave-up for their final album, 2023’s Pure Music. articles.title: Steps review – Netflix’s Disney-lite Cinderella rework has enough pep in its step
articles.summary: The plot might be a little overstuffed and the animation style could be a little more distinctive, but this is better than the streamer’s average animated offering Stop me if you’ve heard this one before, but that age-old story you think you know, well, you might not know it at all. It’s a tale as old as Shrek, which was by no means the first film to subvert fairytale expectations, but it was definitely the most influential, and we’re still feeling its impact 25 years later, for better or worse. What if that villain wasn’t actually the villain after all? What if that love interest shouldn’t have been of interest in the first place? What if that damsel in distress was given a bullet-speed fight scene instead of weeping in a tower?
